=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py, `_verify_run`, lines 876-880 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Run verification does not compare the API-returned run name against the `Failed workflow` field the heal intake embeds in the issue body at `workflow_failure_heal.py:1628-1629`. An unrelated same-repository run on a matching head SHA and branch with a PR link could pass all current checks (repo, SHA, branch, PR, conclusion) and trigger `collect_run()` which fetches jobs, logs, and artifacts with GH_PAT.
  WHY: The `run` object from `gh api repos/<repo>/actions/runs/<id>` already carries `"name"` (used at line 873 for `pr_named`), and the heal issue body carries `- **Failed workflow:** \`<name>\``. A `trusted_run_refs`-extracted `workflow_name` field or a `_verify_run` signature parameter that receives the reported workflow from the `collect` call-site could gate this, but neither exists. An attacker who can reference a same-SHA run from the same repo but a different workflow family (e.g. a `ci.yml` run at the same commit as a `review_autofix.yml` run) would have its logs read.
- changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md, line 1 (category marker `<!-- changelog: added -->`) and line 19 (contributor section) | severity=NIT | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The last-run diff deleted `changelog.d/6215-heal-evidence-run-provenance.md`, a standalone fragment with category marker `<!-- changelog: security -->`, and moved its prose (cross-repository run-provenance verification) into this fragment's contributor note. The #6055 fragment carries `<!-- changelog: added -->`. When `scripts/assemble_changelog.py` groups fragments by category marker and inserts them into `CHANGELOG.md`, the cross-repository security rule will land under the "Added" section instead of "Security".
  WHY: Operators and consumers scanning the "Security" section for the bound-run rule will not find it there after the release assembly runs. The N+1 PR that ships this also adds `changelog.d/6328-heal-evidence-same-repo-run-binding.md` (correctly marked `<!-- changelog: fixed -->`) covering same-repo binding, but neither fragment carries the cross-repo security rule under its proper category marker.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Verify every run, including same-repository runs, against API metadata and the reported failure's issue or PR, head, and workflow before fetching jobs or artifacts."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py, _verify_run (line 876-880) plus trusted_run_refs (line 592) or the collect call-site (line 1200)
  Evidence of absence: _verify_run checks repo, head SHA, branch, PR-linked/named, and conclusion but does not compare `run.get("name")` against the `Failed workflow` value the heal intake embeds in the issue body. The PR diff adds only a docstring comment; no hunk introduces workflow-name extraction from the issue body into a ref field, nor a comparison in _verify_run. The run's `"name"` is already read at line 873 for `pr_named` checks, so the data path exists; the comparison is simply absent.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py, `_verify_run`, lines 850-882 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The new same-repository run binding rule added by #6328 does not compare the run's workflow identity against the heal issue's `Failed workflow` field. The code only verifies `source_repo == repo`, `head_sha`, `head_branch` (or `pr_number`), and `repository.full_name`. An unrelated same-repo run on the reported head SHA and branch (e.g. any default-branch workflow dispatch, where every workflow shares the same head SHA and branch) passes verification. `collect_run` then fetches its jobs, logs, and artifacts with `GH_PAT`.
  WHY: The reporter writes `Failed workflow: <workflow_name>` into every heal issue body (workflow_failure_heal.py:1628-1629), but `heal_context()` does not extract it (workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:561-580) and `_verify_run()` does not pass any expected workflow identity to `gh.json("repos/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}")`. The returned run dict carries `name` (the workflow run name) but the code never compares it. An outside commenter can craft a heal issue with a same-repo run link whose head SHA matches but whose workflow is unrelated (or whose `[pr:N]` name tag was deliberately chosen to match); verification succeeds and the next GH_PAT call reads its jobs, logs, and artifacts.
- changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md, line 19 contributor section | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The contributor note states "Each stage collects its own evidence; nothing is cached between stages." `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py::test_a_later_stage_reuses_completed_runs` (line 653) proves the opposite: a second-stage collector on a shared `tmp_path` reuses completed runs from the first stage's `evidence/runs/` directory, asserts no further API calls to those runs' jobs/artifacts, and confirms "reused from an earlier stage" appears in `INDEX.md`.
  WHY: Operators reading the contributor note will infer the wrong per-stage API budget; an attacker auditing the documented behaviour against the implemented behaviour will find a contradiction and may distrust other parts of the same fragment.
- changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md, full file | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The previous autofix run modified `changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md`, a fragment keyed to issue #6055, while the PR for #6328 is the change under review. The changelog.d/ invariant (CLAUDE.md §20) is one fragment per PR so concurrent PRs cannot collide on `CHANGELOG.md`; editing another PR's fragment breaks that invariant. The same-repo binding rule is now duplicated across `changelog.d/6055-heal-evidence-bundle.md` (in #6055's contributor note) and `changelog.d/6328-heal-evidence-same-repo-run-binding.md` (the PR's own `fixed` fragment). When release assembly folds fragments into `CHANGELOG.md`, both copies land in the consumer-visible entry.
  WHY: If #6055's PR is still open, the in-PR edit to its fragment can conflict with the editor that finalises #6055, and the duplicated content is the wrong category marker (`added` vs `fixed`) for the security finding. If #6055's PR has already merged and the fragment is a leftover (unassembled), the edit is a no-op for CHANGELOG but pollutes the in-tree fragment.
- changelog.d/6215-heal-evidence-run-provenance.md, file deleted by previous autofix run | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The previous autofix run deleted `changelog.d/6215-heal-evidence-run-provenance.md`, a fragment keyed to issue #6215. The #6328 PR's own fragment (`fixed`) does not subsume #6215's `security` entry; the cross-repository binding rule is a separate class of evidence-binding change that has its own `<!-- changelog: security -->` category and its own changelog entry.
  WHY: If #6215's PR is still open and the fragment has not yet been assembled, the deletion silently drops its changelog record. If #6215's PR has merged and the fragment is a leftover, the deletion is a no-op because `assemble_changelog.py` removes assembled fragments on its own.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Verify every run, including same-repository runs, against API metadata and the reported failure's issue or PR, head, and workflow before fetching jobs or artifacts."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py — `heal_context()` (lines 561-580) should extract the `Failed workflow` field from the heal issue body, and `_verify_run()` (lines 850-882) should compare the run's `name` (or `workflow_id`) against that field before returning a verified result.
  Evidence of absence: The PR's diff adds `source_repo`, `head_sha`, and branch/PR checks in `_verify_run()` (PR diff hunk at `scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:848-856`) but adds no workflow identity check. The reporter writes the workflow name into the heal issue body at `scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:1628-1629`; `heal_context()` does not read it (the returned dict has no `workflow_name` key), and `_verify_run()` never compares a returned run's `name` field against any expected workflow. The new tests in `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py` (e.g. `test_same_repo_default_branch_review_run_is_accepted_with_pr_token` at line 778) accept runs based on `[pr:N]` name tags without verifying the workflow identity itself.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
